items.title: The 107 records created from the CultureMech residual have no ingredient_type
items.body:
Found in adversarial review of #505.

All 107 records created by `create_records_from_groundings.py` have no
`ingredient_type`. The field is not schema-required, so nothing failed -- but it is
what `WHOLE_MEDIUM_TYPES` and the NAMED_MEDIUM / UNDEFINED_MIXTURE /
SINGLE_INGREDIENT routing key off, and several of the new records are plainly not
single ingredients:

```
MICRO:0001715  Artificial seawater
MICRO:0000520  Clarified rumen fluid
MICRO:0000521  Sludge fluid
MICRO:0001598  Hemin solution
MICRO:0000456  trace metals 44
MICRO:0000567  Heart Infusion Agar
```

`classify_ingredient_type.py` lives in culturebotai-claw and is the writer for this
field, so filling it is a cross-repo run rather than something #505 should do inline
-- and claw is the repo that would otherwise overwrite whatever MIM wrote (the #148
pattern).

Until it runs, any consumer that filters on `ingredient_type` silently excludes these
107 records. `cross_reference_culturemech.py` is one such consumer: its
`WHOLE_MEDIUM_TYPES` filter is how #490 came to return a confident 0 candidates.

items.title: Verify MICRO:0000520 (clarified rumen fluid) before applying microbedecoder residual decomposition
items.body:
From the review of PR #202 (deep-research groundings for the microbedecoder residual).

Six of the seven "repo convention" biological/complex CURIEs asserted in `mappings/microbedecoder_residual_research_decomposition.tsv` are confirmed already used in `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` (Trypticase peptone MICRO:0000175, casitone MICRO:0000606, horse serum MICRO:0001235, carboxymethylcellulose CHEBI:85146, meat-cooked FOODON:03305103, D-gluconate CHEBI:18391).

**The exception: `MICRO:0000520` "clarified rumen fluid" appears in zero repo records.** It is used in three proposed decomposition rows (`PY-glucose-rumen Fluid`, `PYG + Rumen Fluid`, `Casitone + Yeast Extract + Rumen Fluid`) and one complex-medium row (`Fermented Rumen Extract`). The research agent already flagged rumen fluid as having no exact term and recommended it as a `broadMatch` only, but the specific CURIE was not independently confirmed against OLS/MICRO.

**Action before applying:** confirm `MICRO:0000520` exists in the MICRO ontology and is labelled "clarified rumen fluid" (or find the correct term / UBERON:0010228 ruminal fluid), and decide whether to mint a `kgmicrobe.compound:`/placeholder for rumen fluid as the report's next-steps section suggests. Same open question applies to corn steep liquor (no FOODON/CHEBI term) and the TYGVS VFA mixture.

Related: #200 (chebi.db accession-ceiling refresh, which unblocks the 6 out-of-coverage antibiotics in the same PR).

items.title: Component ids can reference CURIEs MIM has no record for
items.body:
Found during the adversarial review of #366, which made the first use of `IngredientRecord.components`.

Two component identifiers point at CURIEs that are real but have **no corresponding MIM record**:

| component_id | component_name | appears in |
|---|---|---|
| `MICRO:0000520` | clarified rumen fluid | 4 blends |
| `cas:66071-94-1` | corn steep liquor | 1 blend |

Both come from the curated decomposition file and both look correct as identifiers — `MICRO:0000520` was explicitly verified in #204 before that file was applied. The gap is that MIM holds no record for either, so a consumer resolving `components[].component_id` against MIM gets a miss.

## Why it matters

`components` is the mechanism by which a blend is supposed to resolve to its constituents. If a constituent id does not resolve within MIM, the decomposition is only partly traversable — `Casitone + Yeast Extract + Rumen Fluid` resolves two of three constituents to records and the third to a dangling CURIE.

## Options

1. **Create the missing records.** `clarified rumen fluid` (4 uses) and `corn steep liquor` are both real media ingredients that plausibly deserve records; this makes the graph closed.
2. **Accept dangling ids and document it** — `component_id` is a CURIE, not necessarily a MIM foreign key, and pointing at a valid MICRO/CAS term is not wrong.
3. **Add a check** that reports component ids with no MIM record, so the count is visible rather than discovered.

(1) plus (3) seems right: create the two records, and gate the class so the next decomposition pass cannot quietly add more.

Note the schema does not state whether `component_id` is a foreign key into MIM or a free CURIE — worth settling in the slot description either way, since that decides whether a dangling id is a defect or expected.

items.title: CHEBI grounding pass — results, curation report & open follow-ups
items.body:
A CHEBI-grounding pass over MIM's ungrounded ingredients (CAS→CHEBI via the local ChEBI dbxref index, complex-ingredient resolver, non-chemical flagging), relying on MIM's curated data + kg-microbe. **Finding: MIM is already well-curated** — of ~2,206 ungrounded unified rows, the substantive results were a handful of corrections, not a mass grounding.

## Landed (reviewed clean by Fable 5)
- **PR #112** — CHEBI grounding + curation:
  - Gepotidacin `cas:1075236-89-3` → `CHEBI:747127` (skos:exactMatch; unique CAS dbxref + label-exact).
  - Glycogen from bovine liver: `cas:` FALLBACK → `CHEBI:28087` (glycogen), exactMatch (source qualifier).
  - Beef extract: removed erroneous `cas_rn 103-47-9` (that CAS is CHES / `CHEBI:44302` — a PubChem name-lookup false positive); stays on `FOODON:03302088`.
  - SSSOM reconciled in-sync; invariants A/B1/B2/B3 pass.
- **PR #113** — periodic `UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` refresh (3,853→3,937 rows, CHEBI 1,647→1,668). Reviewer confirmed 100% CHEBI internal consistency.

## Already-correct (curation queue items that needed no change)
- sn-glycerol-3-phosphate lithium salt → `CHEBI:15978` (NARROW_MATCH, matches sibling salts).
- carnitine-DL-HCl → `CHEBI:17126` (carnitine, stereo-unspecified parent — correct for a DL racemate).

## Open follow-ups
- [ ] **Audit PubChem-sourced `cas_rn` for other false-positives.** Beef extract's `103-47-9` (=CHES) was a name-lookup mis-assignment by `fetch_cas_rn_from_pubchem`. Cross-check `chemical_properties.cas_rn` (esp. on `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE`/complex records) against CHEBI/expected formula to catch other bad CAS.
- [ ] **45 flagged non-chemicals** need disposition (not CHEBI-groundable): ~10 placeholders ("See source for composition"), ~20 complex mixtures/solutions, ~7 environmental/media, ~8 buffers (borderline). Decide: leave UNMAPPED, map to FOODON/ENVO, or mark NON_CHEMICAL.
- [ ] **Complex-resolver NO_HIT peptones** (Peptone, Proteose peptone, Trypticase peptone, …) would map cleanly to **MICRO** (`MICRO:0000178` = peptone) — deferred; needs the `MICRO:` prefix added to the SSSOM curie_map + builder.
- [ ] **Possible pre-existing mis-mapping:** `Carnitine Hydrochloride` → `CHEBI:48601` "carnitinamide chloride" — carnitinamide is the amide (a different compound); a curator should confirm vs carnitine/carnitinium chloride.

Full pipeline report (per-tier counts, all candidates) is captured in PR #112's description. Spec + report live in the session scratchpad (`GROUNDING_SPEC.md`, `chebi_grounding_report.md`).
